explanation: The M46I mutation reduces nelfinavir binding through a subtle loss of favorable van der Waals interactions in the S1/S1' subpocket. Methionine's longer, flexible sulfur-containing side chain provides more extensive hydrophobic surface area and conformational adaptability to maximize contacts with the inhibitor at the critical 2.4 Å minimum distance, whereas isoleucine's branched aliphatic side chain is more rigid and sterically constrained, creating a suboptimal fit. This modest decrease in binding complementarity—despite negligible overall volume change—demonstrates that inhibitor recognition depends not just on space-filling capacity but on the precise shape and flexibility of contact surfaces within this conserved binding pocket.
